sections.title: Basic Concept of Surds and Indices
sections.content: Indices (powers) and Surds (roots) are important parts of mathematics. Indices represent the power of a number such as a^2, a^3, etc. Surds are roots that cannot be simplified into a rational number, such as √2. Step 1: Identify the power or root in the expression. Step 2: Apply the rules of indices. Step 3: Simplify the expression to obtain the final answer.

sections.title: Multiplication Rule of Indices
sections.content: Step 1: If the base is the same, add the powers. Step 2: Apply the formula a^m × a^n = a^(m+n). Step 3: Simplify the result. Example: 2^3 × 2^4 = 2^(3+4) = 2^7 = 128.

sections.title: Power of a Power Rule
sections.content: Step 1: If a power is raised to another power, multiply the powers. Step 2: Apply the formula (a^m)^n = a^(m×n). Step 3: Simplify the expression. Example: (3^2)^3 = 3^(2×3) = 3^6.

sections.title: Comparison of Surds
sections.content: Step 1: Try to convert all numbers to the same power form. Step 2: If necessary, raise them to a common power so that the roots can be eliminated. Step 3: Compare the resulting numbers normally. Example: To compare √2, ∛3, and ∜4, they can all be raised to power 12.

sections.title: Simple Exponential Equations
sections.content: Step 1: Convert both sides into the same base. Step 2: Compare the powers. Step 3: Solve for the variable. Example: 2^(x+3) = 32. Step 1: 32 = 2^5. Step 2: x+3 = 5. Step 3: x = 2.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Applying the power addition rule incorrectly. 2. Adding powers even when the bases are different. 3. Directly guessing answers while comparing surds. 4. Not converting bases to the same base in exponential equations.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: The main rules of indices include addition and multiplication of powers with the same base. In surds, creating a common power helps in comparison. In exponential equations, converting both sides to the same base makes solving easier.

tricks.title: Same Base Addition Rule
tricks.explanation: If the base is the same, add the powers.

tricks.title: Power Multiply Rule
tricks.explanation: If a power is raised to another power, multiply the powers.

tricks.title: Division Rule
tricks.explanation: If the bases are the same in division, subtract the powers.

tricks.title: Convert Root to Power
tricks.explanation: Roots can be converted into fractional powers.

tricks.title: Surd Comparison Trick
tricks.explanation: Raise all numbers to a common power and then compare them.

tricks.title: Perfect Power Recognition
tricks.explanation: Memorize common perfect powers to simplify quickly.

tricks.title: Base Equal Method
tricks.explanation: In exponential equations, make the bases equal on both sides.

tricks.title: Even Root Logic
tricks.explanation: When taking an even root, consider the positive principal value.
